title: MasterFabric · Airflow MLOps
tagline: Replays a year of telco churn modeling on Airflow, MLflow, Evidently and Feast with measured retraining results.
summary: MasterFabric Airflow MLOps replays a full year of a simulated telco churn pipeline on a single laptop, using Airflow to land monthly subscriber snapshots, gate them on data quality, measure realised performance once labels arrive, check feature drift, and decide whether to retrain. Promotion is implemented as an MLflow registry alias that a FastAPI service follows without a restart, so champion and challenger models can be swapped live. Evidently supplies a second opinion on drift and realised quality each month, Feast serves the same features to training and to the online API, and a new champion is rolled out through a sticky canary with pre-declared guardrails. The project checks its own claims against two references, a model that is never retrained and the data generator's own true churn probabilities, with every number measured on runs on an Apple M4 Pro with Docker through Colima.
keyResults: Backfill: 12 monthly runs (2025-12 to 2026-11), all successful, 60,000 to 66,274 subscribers, 1.2-8.4 s of task time per month
Realised AUC, 2026-10: auto policy (v4) 0.830 vs never retrained (v1) 0.789, oracle upper bound 0.841
Top-decile lift, 2026-10: auto 4.98 vs never retrained 4.63
Drift signal: PSI of plan 0.3151 vs v1's data when postpaid_5g appeared, against a trigger of 0.25
Online API: p50 2.67 ms, p95 2.93 ms per subscriber; 1,000 rows scored in 11.4 ms; max difference to batch scores 5.0e-6
Rollback: @champion moved from v4 to v3 served after 3.41 s, and back to v4 after 15.27 s (15 s poll), with no restart
Evidently vs in-house PSI: default detector flags 3-7 of 16 columns in all 6 monitored months; the PSI > 0.25 trigger agrees in 5 of 6 months; realised AUC identical (delta 0.0)
Feast point-in-time: 0 of 194,913 training rows differ from the hand-written join, while a naive latest-snapshot join leaves all 11,179 churners without features
Canary rollout: shuffled-label v6 rolled back at 5% (Spearman -0.088); v5 passed 5/25/50% stages, paired delta AUC -0.0007 [-0.0031, +0.0016], and was promoted

Root-cause report: v6 re-rolled against champion v5 was rolled back again at 5% (Spearman -0.073), and the report took 2.1 s; of six hypotheses only model signal (holdout AUC 0.4414) and training labels were supported, with the verdict label corruption in the training job
Root-cause control: retrained from v6's own lineage tags the recipe scores 0.8297 while the registered artefact scores 0.4414 (0.4484 on its own training labels); for v5 all hypotheses were ruled out

Drift watcher replay over 40,000 served subscribers: a sustained plan breach (PSI 0.266 at 20,000, sustained at 22,500) retrained v10, which was rejected (0.7816 vs v1 0.7819); with 2026-08 traffic and labels up to 2026-07, v11 was promoted (0.819 vs 0.7796) and served 4.1 s later
Drift watcher reached exactly the models the monthly DAG built (v10 = v2, v11 = v3); a retrain plus registration took 3.5 to 3.7 s and a run without retraining 2.5 s
limitations: The subscriber base, drift and broken feed are all generated synthetically, so the generator sets the ceiling for how much retraining can help; the mechanics (gate, triggers, promotion, serving) are what transfer, not the exact AUC numbers
Results come from a single deterministic run (seed 42); thresholds like PSI 0.25, decay 0.03 and gain 0.002 were set from domain defaults rather than tuned on this run
The final 2026-11 month was triggered by hand rather than waiting for the real monthly schedule
Training runs inside the Airflow worker itself, which is fine at this data scale but would need to move to a separate job at operator scale
The lake uses pandas and parquet rather than Spark and Iceberg, keeping the repo small and readable by design
The serving API relies on polling (checks aliases every 15 s) rather than events, since open-source MLflow 2.22 has no registry webhooks
Lab-grade security: services bind to localhost only, credentials are lab placeholders, MLflow and the API have no authentication, and the S3 store is single-node
The canary rollout replays a single past month's traffic in minutes rather than real traffic arriving over weeks with labels a month later
Only one rollout was exercised, with one obviously broken candidate and one normal one; a subtler failure such as a single shifted feature was not tested
No business metric is computed; AUC and top-decile lift stand in for retention value rather than a priced uplift evaluation

The rollout moved @champion outside the DAG: v5 was promoted by scripts/rollout.py, so the decisions table still ends at v4 and the promotion is recorded in registry tags and docs/results/rollout.json
The evidently_report and publish_features tasks were run for the 12 existing months with airflow tasks test after the backfill, which records no task state

Evidently's numeric PSI is not the DAG's PSI: it uses equal-width bins while the in-house PSI uses reference deciles, so they agree on categorical columns and on the trigger in 5 of 6 months, not on every numeric value
Feast runs on files: the offline store is one parquet file rewritten each month and the registry is a local file, and training still uses the hand-written join that Feast was shown to match

The root-cause report covers six hypotheses and was tested on one injected incident (shuffled labels) and one healthy control; a segment-only failure or an online/offline feature mismatch is not among its checks, and its deciding check retrains, which is seconds here and can be hours at scale

The drift watcher was exercised by replay with airflow dags test after every 2,500 subscribers, not by the scheduler, so every 10 minutes was not measured in wall time; it added model versions 7 to 11 to the registry
